title: Vulnerability triage + threat modeling workshop notes — 2026-05-12
content:
Attendees: Ava (host), Marcus, Lina, Ravi, Evelyn, Jamal, + notes from SRE on call
Duration: 75m (standup + 45m focused triage + 20m threat-modeling breakout)
Location: #sec-eng weekly, recording -> CONFLUENCE-12345

Agenda:
- Quick status review: outstanding high/critical vulns
- Deep-dive: three prioritized findings from automated scans and one manual report
- Secrets review: recent findings from gitguardian + internal detector
- Threat-modeling mini-workshop: Dedicated pools + KV cache exposure scenarios
- Action item assignment & owners

Summary / Decisions (TL;DR):
- Prioritize SEC-2026-147 (runtime token exposure) and SEC-2026-152 (third-party lib with crypto flaw). Both moved to "hotfix" path.
- Secrets: rotate 3 keys (aws/redwood-prod-ops, pg-readonly, analytics-ingest). Automate rotation and block commit history in CI.
- Threat model: add pre-deployment sandboxing for model tool-calling; require deny-listing for function calls in hosted API for public routes.
- Followups: create runbook for KV-cache purge and short-term mitigation for cached prefix leakage.

Triage details (notes + decisions):
1) SEC-2026-147 — "Kv cache prefix leak in continuous batching"
   - Source: internal fuzzer + customer report (partial prompt leakage observed in reused cache windows)
   - Affected: serving-runtime (continuous batching / prefix reuse), hosted API and dedicated pools using shared cache config
   - Severity: High (potential PII exposure in aggregated traffic)
   - Repro steps: run multi-tenant concurrent prompts with long-prefix overlap > 4096 tokens; observe cross-request KV hits in logs
   - Immediate mitigation: turn off prefix reuse for multi-tenant hosted pools (config toggle), add per-request partitioning flag; applied to canary region eu-west-1 by SRE (Marcus)
   - Long-term fix: implement stricter namespace isolation in KV keys + HMAC per-request key derivation by runtime team (owner: Ravi)
   - ETA: hotfix config applied 2026-05-12; full fix target 2026-06-02
   - Status: in_progress

2) SEC-2026-152 — "crypto library deprecation (libcrypto-x < 3.2.1)"
   - Source: dependency scan (Snyk) + vendor advisory
   - Affected: private-deployments installer image and some internal CLI tools
   - Severity: Critical (RCE vector in old lib path)
   - Decision: urgent image rebuild + CI gates to fail builds using vulnerable deps
   - Owner: Lina (platform-eng liaison) to coordinate images; Security to validate
   - ETA: image rebuild by 2026-05-14; enforced gating 2026-05-20
   - Status: assigned

3) SEC-2026-159 — "exposed S3 creds in archived logs (old archive bucket)"
   - Source: manual audit + GitGuardian historical scan
   - Affected: logs-archival pipeline and archived blobs; keys belong to older demo account
   - Severity: Medium
   - Mitigation: rotate keys + search-and-erase archive; add lifecycle policy to auto-expire demo keys in 30d; blocked immediate public access (Evelyn)
   - Owner: Evelyn Park
   - ETA: rotate 2026-05-13; archive scrub 2026-05-20
   - Status: remediation_planned

Secrets & CI notes:
- GitGuardian run found 3 hits in feature branches: aws/redwood-prod-ops (exposed in test fixture), pg-readonly, analytics-ingest.
- Short-term: disable branches with confirmed leaks; rotate keys and add to KMS with automatic rotation policy.
- CI: add a pre-commit hook and a CircleCI job to fail on credentials plus mask token outputs in logs. (Owner: Jamal)
- Hardening: add rules to secret-detector to flag base64-encoded AWS access patterns and to ignore well-formed KMS ARNs.
- Note to self: add a scheduled weekly secret-scan report to #sec-alerts (automate via internal lambda).

Threat-modeling breakout (20m) — notes and outcomes:
- Focus area: Dedicated pools + model rollouts + function-calling surface
- Threat: prompt-injection that triggers function-calls (exfil via downstream webhook)
  - Proposed control: require function-call schemas be white-listed in the console; by default restrict tool-calls for public endpoints unless route-level opt-in.
  - Owner: Product security + Console team (Ravi + Lina)
- Threat: KV-cache leak (discussed above)
  - Control: per-tenant namespaces + short TTL for cached items + enforced content-sanitization for any cacheable payloads. Also add an assertion check on retrieval to ensure requester identity matches cache owner.
  - Owner: Serving runtime (Ravi)
- Threat: model hallucination exposing sensitive system prompts or policy content
  - Control: move sensitive system prompts into encrypted KMS stores and fetch at inference time; never write system prompts into persistent logs. Add masking in observability UI.
  - Owner: Product + Observability (Marcus)

Action items (concrete):
- AVA-1: Publish hotfix summary and notify larger PM/CS (Ava) — due 2026-05-12 (DONE)
- RAVI-1: Implement KV key HMAC scheme + per-request namespace enforcement (Ravi) — target 2026-06-02
- LINA-1: Rebuild private-deploy images, add CI gating for libcrypto (Lina) — target 2026-05-14
- EVELYN-1: Rotate archived S3 keys and scrub old archive (Evelyn) — target 2026-05-20
- JAMAL-1: Add pre-commit secret hook + CI secret-scan job; push to all repos (Jamal) — target 2026-05-18
- MARCUS-1: Add telemetry for cache hit owner and alert on cross-tenant cache reads (Marcus) — target 2026-05-21
- SECURITY-Ops: Draft runbook for KV-cache purge (playbook outline + rollback steps) — owner: sec-ops crew; publish by 2026-05-15

Open questions / parking lot:
- How to signal to Dedicated customers when we flip on per-tenant namespace (migration window + performance impact)? (Product stake needed)
- Do we need an SLA change/notice for hosted API users for the short-term config where prefix reuse is disabled? (Legal/Comms)
- Can we add a lightweight smoke test in the canary for KV isolation without full perf regression? (SRE)

Notes-to-self / informal bits:
- Ran quick local repro for SEC-2026-147; not purely deterministic — needs a high-concurrency harness. Consider using k6 to reproduce at scale.
- Found an unrelated lint failure in the private-deploy repo while trying to run image rebuild; raise separate ticket.

Next meeting: weekly sec-eng triage — 2026-05-19 10:00 PT; propose 30m focused triage (only high/critical) + async updates to Confluence for in-progress items.

Appendix (useful refs):
- Fuzzer report excerpt: CONFLUENCE-12345#fuzzer-excerpt
- Dependency advisory: https://snyk.io/advisories/crypto-x-3.2.0
- GitGuardian scan run (summary): internal:GG-2026-05-11
- Runbook stub: internal:kv-purge-runbook-v0

End notes: meeting tone was productive. Keep momentum on hotfix + image rebuild. If owners see blockers, call out in #sec-eng ASAP.
